references.text: In [ref:Prov 11:31|Proverbs 11:31] it says: "If the righteous are repaid on earth, how much more will the wicked and the sinner!" This is likely the Old Testament background for Jesus' words. If the green tree (the innocent) is treated this way, what will happen to the dry tree (the guilty)?
In [ref:Ezek 20:47|Ezekiel 20:47] God uses the image of fire that consumes both green and dry trees as a picture of judgment. Jesus applies similar imagery concerning the green and the dry tree.

In [ref:Ezek 17:24|Ezekiel 17:24] the Lord speaks of making the green tree dry and the dry tree green. The image of the green versus the dry tree is used as an expression of God's judgment and restoration, forming the background for Jesus' metaphor.

[ref:1 Pet 4:17–18|1 Peter 4:17–18] expresses the same thought: "For it is time for judgment to begin with the household of God. But if it begins with us, what will be the end for those who do not obey the gospel of God?" Peter applies the same logic as Jesus: if the righteous suffer, how much worse will it be for the ungodly.

The context in [ref:Luke 23:28–30|Luke 23:28–30] shows that Jesus' words are directed to the women of Jerusalem who weep over him, and he warns of the coming judgment on Jerusalem. Verse 31 summarizes this with the image of the green and the dry tree.

In [ref:Isa 10:16–19|Isaiah 10:16–19] God's judgment is described as a fire that consumes both thornbushes and forests, including imagery of trees being destroyed. Jesus' image of the dry tree burning more easily has parallels to this prophecy of judgment.
